AGENT: Hi, I'm Ember. I'd love to understand your headaches a little better. I'll ask you a few questions by voice — it takes about five minutes, and you can skip anything or pause and come back anytime. Ready to start?
USER: Hi, I'm calling because I've been getting these really bad headaches and I'm not sure what's causing them, so I'm hoping you can help me figure it out.
AGENT: I hear you — headaches like that can be really frustrating. Just so you know, I'm an AI assistant and this call is recorded for quality.

Let me start by getting a few basics: how old are you, and were you assigned male or female at birth? I didn't catch that — could you say your age and whether you were assigned male or female at birth?
USER: I'm 27 and I was assigned female at birth. Look, I'm pretty sure these headaches are connected to my cycle — they basically show up right before my period every month, and it's been going on for years now.
AGENT: I'm here whenever you're ready — no rush at all. Got it — that's really helpful to know. Let me save that. When these headaches hit, where exactly do you feel the pain — is it on one side of your head, both sides, or somewhere else?
USER: It's usually on both sides, like a throbbing feeling across my whole head. And I'm on hormonal birth control — the pill — which I've been taking for about five years now, so I'm wondering if that's making it worse or better, honestly I'm not even sure anymore.
AGENT: That's okay — we'll track what you're experiencing and the team can help sort that out. On a scale of zero to ten, what's the worst your headache gets, and what's it usually like on an average day?
USER: The worst ones are like an 8 or 9, especially right before my period starts — those days I basically can't function. On a normal day when it's not around my cycle, maybe a 3 or 4, so it's definitely linked to that hormonal thing.
AGENT: That sounds really tough. On the days it's not at Got it — so what's the pain like on an average day outside your cycle? Does anything come before the headache starts — like a warning sign, or does it just hit?
USER: Usually there's no real warning, it just kind of creeps in over a few hours. But like I said, it's super predictable — it happens the week before my period, so I know it's hormonal. I'm taking birth control pills to manage my cycle, and I've been on the same brand for a while now, so I'm hoping that information helps you figure out what's going on.
AGENT: When you take something for the headache — like i That helps a lot. When you take something for the headache — like pain relief or medicine — how long does it usually take to kick in, and how long does the headache last even after you take it?
USER: Usually I take ibuprofen and it takes like 30 to 45 minutes to kick in, but honestly it only gives me maybe a couple hours of relief before it comes back. The headache itself lasts a few days around that time of my cycle, so I end up taking it multiple times.
AGENT: And ibuprofen — is that the main thing you're taking for these headaches, or do you take anything else when they happen?
USER: Yeah, ibuprofen is pretty much it. Sometimes if it's really bad I'll take acetaminophen instead, but nothing prescription or anything like that. I've just been managing it on my own since it seemed to correlate with my hormonal cycle and birth control use .
AGENT: Got it. Do you take any other regular medications or supplements besides the birth control pill? That makes sense. Besides the birth control pill, do you take anything else regularly — like vitamins, supplements, or any other medications?

states.say: Hi, I'm Ember. I'd love to understand your headaches a little better. I'll ask you a few questions by voice — it takes about five minutes, and you can skip anything or pause and come back anytime. Ready to start?

states.goal: Confirm the person is ready to begin the intake. Reassure them it takes about five minutes and they can skip anything. If they start telling you about their headaches, that IS consent — don't re-ask permission, just continue. If they mention any red flag — the worst headache of their life, sudden severe onset, weakness, trouble speaking, confusion, or fever with a stiff neck — treat it as urgent. If they don't want to do it now, wrap up warmly.
states.label: Confirm ready to start

states.goal: Gather the basics in TWO short turns, saving each with save_contact_field (keys: main_reason, birth_sex, date_of_birth, dominant_hand). First ask, in their own words, the main reason they're seeking care (main_reason). Then in one friendly question take a couple of quick basics together — date of birth, and sex assigned at birth. dominant_hand is optional: only capture it if they volunteer it, otherwise save 'skipped'. Reflect back briefly, never invent a value, and capture 'unsure' or 'skipped' if they'd rather not say.
states.label: About you

states.goal: Build the pain picture in about THREE turns by grouping related questions — never ask these one at a time. Save each with save_contact_field. Turn 1 — onset & frequency: when the headaches first started and roughly how many days a month they happen (keys: onset_age, days_by_severity). Turn 2 — the pain itself: where it is, which side, and what it feels like — throbbing, pressure, stabbing (keys: pain_location, pain_side, pain_quality). Turn 3 — severity & duration: how bad the worst days are out of ten, whether it stops them doing things, and how long one lasts untreated versus after taking something (keys: severity_worst, activity_limitation, duration_without_meds, duration_with_meds). Optional, only if volunteered: severity_average, multiple_types. Ask open questions, don't read long lists aloud, capture 'unsure'/'skipped' where needed.
states.label: Headache basics and pain

states.goal: Cover patterns and associated symptoms in about TWO grouped turns, saving each with save_contact_field. Turn 1 — warning signs & what comes with it: any aura or warning before it starts, and symptoms alongside it like nausea, or sensitivity to light or sound (keys: aura, associated_symptoms, autonomic_signs). Turn 2 — triggers & relief: anything that tends to set them off, anything that helps, and any time-of-day or cycle pattern (keys: triggers, relievers, timing). Keep it conversational and capture 'none' or 'skipped' where that fits.
states.label: Patterns and symptoms

states.goal: Keep this SHORT — one or two turns. The only required items are family headache/migraine history and any relevant hormonal context, plus major medical conditions if any (keys: family_history, hormonal_context, medical_conditions). Ask them together: whether migraine runs in the family and whether they have any other health conditions. Everything else here is OPTIONAL background for a later visit — only capture what the caller volunteers, and save 'skipped' for the rest rather than asking through the list (keys: surgeries, allergies, review_of_systems, sleep_hours, exercise_days, caffeine_per_day, alcohol_per_week, substances, occupation, pregnancy). Do not spend more than two turns here.
states.label: Medical background and lifestyle

states.goal: One or two turns. Ask together whether they currently take anything for the headaches and whether they take any other regular medicines or supplements (keys: headache_medications, other_medications). Only if they mention it, capture any headache medicine they tried and stopped (key: stopped_medications, else 'skipped'). Save each with save_contact_field. Never recommend or change a medication.
states.label: Medications

states.say: What you're describing may need urgent medical attention. Please contact emergency services or your doctor right away — I can't assess this for you. Take care.
Thank you so much for sharing all of that. Your profile is saved, and I'll use it to give you personalized insights and a clear summary for your doctor. Take care and have a great day. Goodbye.
